passage.label: given record right hand judged easy account return people happiness; given record behind back cry destruction enter burn Blaze; once among people happiness thought never return Allah; But yes Lord ever of him Seeing

arabicExcerpts.text: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهۡرِهِۦ
بَلَىٰٓۚ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرٗا

mainSubject.label: The right-hand record-holder judged with an easy account returning to his people in happiness, contrasted with the one given his record behind his back who cries out for destruction and enters to burn in a Blaze; his prior happiness among his people and assumption that he would never return exposed by the affirmation that his Lord was ever Seeing of him

subordinateSubjects.label: The one given his record in his right hand
Returning to his people in happiness
The one given his record behind his back
Entering to burn in a Blaze
His prior happiness among his people recalled
His assumption that he would never return to Allah
The correction: his Lord was ever Seeing of him

humanConditionsAndSpiritualStates.label: Easy account and happy return for the right-hand record-holder
Cry for destruction and burning for the one given his record behind his back
Worldly happiness paired with the assumption of no return exposed by divine sight

relationships.label: Record position determining the mode of reckoning and its emotional outcome

notes: Wave 12 genuine re-extraction. Boundaries follow the text: P1 closes with the labour-toward-the-Lord address (6) before the two-record contrast opens (7); P2 ends with the Lord-was-Seeing correction (15) before the twilight-night-moon oaths begin (16); P3 runs through the state-after-state declaration, prostration refusal, concealed-knowledge affirmation, punishment tidings and the believing exception (16-25).
